summary: Phase 3B — provider-neutral calendar integration: 24/24 backend tests PASSED against the public preview URL. Verified: connection PUT/GET with access_mode (read_write→'connected', read_only→'read_only', invalid→422); /calendar/pending gated correctly (empty when disconnected or read_only, populated when read_write); /calendar/sync links internal↔external, creates calendar_links, removes item from pending, and is idempotent on repeat; /calendar/external/ingest auto-applies title-only edits on non-high-risk study events, queues external_edit review for time changes without mutating the internal event, and queues review for ANY edit on recurring or exam events; /calendar/review/{id} approve applies pending changes, dismiss leaves them; deletion-detection via window creates external_delete review and approval removes the internal event + link; non-SA externals stored in mirror with is_sa=false and never spawn tasks; /calendar/status handles permission_revoked (disconnect), sync_failed with failure_reason persisted, and 422 on invalid status; /briefing?tz_offset_min=0 includes external today with external=true, avoids duplicating SA-linked events, surfaces 'Schedule conflict' risk on overlapping timed events, and adds stats.external_today + stats.calendar_review; two-user isolation confirmed (User B sees no A connection/links/mirror/reviews); regression on tasks/events CRUD + /briefing + /timeline + /reminders all 200; DELETE /me returns 200 for dev-login accounts without password, 403 for password accounts without/with wrong password, and 200 with correct password. No React Native issues to report — this run was backend-only per request.
action_items: None blocking — Phase 3B backend is spec-complete. Device-side flows (expo-calendar reads/writes, provider sync) remain DEVICE-ONLY and MUST NOT be treated as passed based on API tests alone; verify on a native build.
Reminder: the in-memory rate limiter may 429 with rapid repeated /auth/register calls on the same host — the DELETE /me password-account test skips gracefully when it does.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/calendar.py:_is_high_risk_event correctly flags recurring OR event_type=='exam'; ingest branches on this OR any start/end change → matches the 'title-only auto, time/high-risk requires confirmation' spec.

/calendar/sync uses (user_id, internal_id) key on calendar_links with $set upsert → repeated syncs are idempotent (no duplicate link, no error). Confirmed in test_sync_links_event_and_removes_from_pending.
/calendar/pending returns [] unless connected AND access_mode=='read_write' — matches spec exactly.
/briefing correctly excludes is_sa externals from the external_today merge to prevent duplicates, and inserts calendar_review count as an error-level risk (nice UX signal).
DELETE /me safeguard in routers/auth.py checks users.password_hash presence and requires a valid password verify — dev-login accounts (no password_hash) bypass as expected.

Minor: routers/calendar.py external ingest updates db.audit with a 'new' field that only stores ev.title even when the change is start/end — cosmetic, doesn't affect correctness; consider serialising the full change dict.

Minor: /calendar/pending includes ALL unlinked events (even those without a start/end). The current filter drops entries missing 'start', which is fine, but recurring-approval gating relies on 'events not in db.review' being an invariant — worth an explicit comment/test if that ever changes.
seed_data_creation: Each test class opens fresh throwaway dev-login sessions (TEST_<slug>_<uuid8>@example.com). The password-account deletion test registers TEST_pw_<uuid8>@uni.edu, verifies via /auth/dev-outbox, and deletes itself at the end. No persistent seed data left behind beyond user rows those create (which the DELETE /me test also cleans up).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 3B backend is fully green against the public preview URL. Real device-calendar operations (expo-calendar) and actual Google/Microsoft-on-Android sync are DEVICE-ONLY — do NOT mark them passed from API-only runs. When re-running the auth-heavy DELETE /me test on the same host in quick succession, expect occasional 429 (in-memory rate limiter); the suite already `pytest.skip`s in that case. The dev-outbox lowercases the recipient email — match case-insensitively when parsing tokens.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. One transient test-code miss (case-sensitive email compare against dev-outbox) was fixed in the suite itself before finalising.
